items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: In fact one of them was almost the chart that Billy May had written for Nat, it was almost note for note, in like a slightly different key that I did it for Natalie.

ctx.x: Tell me how the recording with Natalie Cole came about. Gee, almost eight, nine years ago?

Well the producer, who was her husband at the time, just called me and said come out to the studio where I’m working and we’ll talk about it. So we talked and he wanted to know about some players to use and talked to me about the music. They were mostly — oh yeah, that was the Nat Cole album, and they were things that Nat had done. So it turns out what he wanted for — I think he wanted me to do four charts — were almost copies of the charts that Nat had done. In fact one of them was almost the chart that Billy…
Were you in on the recording sessions?

items.title: Holman Bill — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I see here Natalie Cole, Unforgettable.

ctx.x: come up with the funniest tunes. One of them was – I think on the first album – was Tico Tico. I think of a lady organ player on The Hit Parade that used to play that, and they‟d always shoot her feet on the pedals. But a jazz chart on Tico Tico? Uh-uh. But I did it, and it came off okay. I wrote some of my best things for that band, I think, in strictly a jazz band vein. Terry – again, the businessman – he wanted a big chord on the end of every chart, whether it called for it or not, regardless of what the song…

That‟s important. Anything else you want to mention? I‟m looking at a couple of names to your credit. I see here Natalie Cole, Unforgettable. That‟s back to the Grammys. And then working with Tony Bennett. I‟m sure that must have been gratifying.

Yeah, it was okay, doing the recording and everything, but when the record came out, he had only used 4 of 11 charts that I did for him, for the Basie band. By the way, I was really happy with the Basie band, because my other experience with them – I told you about them having trouble reading. These guys were on top of all that. So there was no problem there.
